source_build.native_build: nativeRelease -PnativeImageBuildHeap=6g -PnativeImageBuildParallelism=4; default SIZE optimization; compiler budgets do not change application heap
limitations: No real Google account was used for native checks.
Direct GNOME shortcut assignment and held-key behavior were not exercised in the native build.
Legacy Rhino resolver path and Windows native MSI were not revalidated.
Both artifacts require the build host ABI and system libVLC/browser/keyring.

configurations.jvm: OpenJDK 21.0.12.1; packaged jpackage launcher: -Xms32m -Xmx768m; default G1 GC; code cache 128m; ParallelGCThreads=4 ConcGCThreads=2 G1ConcRefinementThreads=4. Heap declared from ArchiveTune.cfg, not detected from argv.
configurations.native: GraalVM Community 25.0.3+9 (25.1.3+9.1); SIZE optimization (-Os), compatibility CPU target, Serial GC, baked-in max heap 128m and MaxHeapFree=16m. Heap declared from build configuration.

limitations: CPU comes from /proc/<pid>/stat deltas polled every sample interval: a helper that lives for less than one interval can be missed, as can its last CPU increment before exit.
CPU percent is relative to one logical core (100% is one fully busy core, not one machine).
The tree RSS total counts a shared page once per process and therefore overstates the physical RAM; PSS divides shared pages among their sharers and USS is the private footprint.
PSS/USS come from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup; without that file the report carries null values instead of a partial total.
Only the tree this harness launched is measured; the user's own instance and other desktop services are excluded from the totals but still consume host resources.
The launcher wrapper (AppImage AppRun, jpackage launcher, shell script) is reported separately from the dominant CPU consumer, which is treated as the application process.
Warmups prime shared host caches; every measured run still has a fresh private XDG tree.
The harness never rewrites a command line: JVM flags and the native heap setting must be documented in arm notes when baked into a launcher or image; both arms must be built from the same source.
Anonymous background maintenance may run; the workload needs no account or DRM and uses a local muted file played through the real playback controller.
This is a process-level measurement: it says nothing about in-app latency or frame rate.
No real Google account was used for native checks.
Direct GNOME shortcut assignment and held-key behavior were not exercised in the native build.
Legacy Rhino resolver path and Windows native MSI were not revalidated.
Both artifacts require the build host ABI and system libVLC/browser/keyring.
Startup measures unpacked launchers; AppImage mounting/extraction time is excluded.
